notes.title: Development Update Feb-May 2025
notes.content: [p]We’re nearly halfway through 2025 – how time flies![/p][p]2025 has been an exciting year for us, with progress on every aspect of the game as we move into the polishing phase of our vertical slice. Our goal with the vertical slice is to demonstrate the look, feel and quality of gameplay, art and narrative you can expect in the final product. We’ll be using the vertical slice for testing and as a promotional tool, not least in outreach to the press.[/p][p]We’re also thrilled to share that, in conjunction with our [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1748280/view/505077075736002667?l=english"]partnership with Templar Media as our publisher[/url], we’ve now teamed up with a professional marketing agency. With their expertise, we’re gearing up to expand Gate Zero’s reach to even more audiences around the world. As we ramp up our marketing efforts towards release, you can expect to see us at major gaming conventions in the coming year![/p][p]Together with our marketing consultants, we are planning a strategic approach to revealing different aspects of the game over time. If you’ve been wondering what we’ve been up to behind the scenes lately, it’s because many of the new gameplay mechanics—one of our main focuses since the release of the Steam prototype—have been intentionally kept under wraps. We’re excited to share more in the time to come as we roll out key marketing beats at carefully planned intervals up until release.[/p][p]For now, here’s what we can share![/p][p][/p][h2]Art[/h2][h3]Capernaum Set Dressing[/h3][p]With level design and architecture far along, our artists are now working on beautifying the environment with details.[/p][p]Here’s what our art director, Mette, considers in the set dressing process:[/p][p][i]“What I always try to convey is a sense that someone actually lived there—the plants, baskets, chairs or crates are placed where they are because people either had an intention with them, or they were on their way from A to B and life just happened.[/i][/p][p][i]I like to think that people in the 1st century also tried to make their surroundings look homey and nice, not just functional. Some flowers on the front porch, a chair to sit outside and greet people, etc.[/i][/p][p][i]And then there’s all the misplaced stuff—things that were just left in an alley way or backyard or along the road and no one picked it up, but it adds to the feeling of life happening. Tiny little stories.[/i][/p][p][i]I try to make unique looks, so even though I may reuse the same 100 or so assets, I try to combine them and make them feel used differently by different people.”[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/5f9d2baa39e5172c3b819991cd4140eb9a159818.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/cafae41676385f2120b5c86f5aa1295750a13c42.jpg"][/img][/p][h2][b]Capernaum Marketplace Assets[/b][/h2][p]And here are some examples of assets being placed out in the Capernaum world.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/242b893998ac7dcc17a6125cd7a6c8d0b7e603bd.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/8277e519dac46b1fbfa5e4c4331f526cd1339ab5.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/1475f68ff74d902261a3f719fc75ba3270d93bf3.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/e06b6738968f1a28f423bac25d28d1276198ed98.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Character Models[/b][/h2][p]The unique characters featured in our vertical slice are coming to life. This is where all of our earlier research into 1st century clothing pays off, as it informs the way we model and express each character’s personality.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/fa4504d54770bcd4e46d7cc10cca9572c39af553.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/ff7858794ed68923f415552395f316d1f95c1639.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Games Mechanics[/h2][h3]Crafting & Light Survival Economy[/h3][p]When you find yourself stuck in a different realm through time travel, what do you do? Learn to survive, of course![/p][p]With that in mind, our game designers have been developing systems such as tool crafting using gathered resources, as well as light survival mechanics reflecting the realities of 1st century life—including the need for food, water and shelter.[/p][p][/p][h2]Audio & Script[/h2][p]Bringing a historically immersive game world to life takes a lot of thoughtful detail.[/p][p]This past month, our writers have been hard at work crafting custom dialogue barks—short one-way statements delivered by Non-Player Characters (NPCs) to add depth and authenticity to the world.[/p][p]We’ve now created around 650 custom dialogue barks, which will be voiced by a wide range of characters—from Roman soldiers and guards to ordinary Capernaum residents including pedestrians, synagogue attendees, market traders and shoppers.[/p][p]This is what game writer, Steve, had to say about the process:[/p][p][i]“For the world to sound as natural and authentic as possible, there has to be a wide variety of ages and backgrounds, and in some cases the NPCs have their own backstory. We want the player to get familiar with characters who live in Capernaum.[/i][/p][p][i]The city was small, around 1,500 inhabitants, and no more than the size of a large, modern-day school, so it’s quite possible most inhabitants knew one another. Although an NPC may be ‘just’ a market trader now, he or she may play a more important role later in the story.”[/i][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="jX2KMRXkoEo;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h2]Animation[/h2][p]We’ve been refining various rigs and animations, with a focus on traversal movements like climbing, sliding, and dodging.[/p][p]In addition, we’re building a wide range of overlay states—such as holding different items—all set up in a modular system. This allows any character to use the same items seamlessly, with animations that automatically adapt to each one.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/0bf66c8f2a0cd4355f990a048e8801792ac8facd.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Bible App – Impact in 2024[/h2][p]Did you know that [url="http://bible.us/r/BbI"]Gate Zero has a Bible reading plan[/url] on the Youversion Bible App that’s translated into 19 languages?[/p][p]Help us continue creating life-changing Bible experiences for the next generation.[/p][p][/p][h3][url="https://nextgenbiblemedia.org/donate/?utm_source=steamupdate&utm_medium=steamupdate&utm_campaign=steamfebmay"]Click here to support Gate Zero with a tax-deductible gift.[/url][/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/81d775398aab36ec82efc2636b3cd098489619cc.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Bible X Announces Partnership with Templar Media
notes.content:
[b]Moss, Norway – March 14, 2025 –[/b] Today, we’re thrilled to announce our partnership with Templar Media, a newly launched video game publisher and media company, to publish [i]Gate Zero[/i], the highly anticipated action/adventure game that transports players to first-century Roman-era Judea.

Founded by 25-year game industry veteran John Gibson, Templar Media will focus on releasing content that puts[i] Entertainment First! [/i]In an entertainment industry that has stumbled in recent years with alienating customers by putting social agendas ahead of entertainment, Templar Media aims to bring entertaining gamers and viewers back into focus. This aligns perfectly with Bible X’s ambition to bring the Bible to life for a new generation of young people.  This collaboration will, among other things, bring [i]Gate Zero[/i] to PC, Xbox, and PlayStation platforms, making it accessible to gamers worldwide.

[h3]THE FUTURE ECHOES IN THE PAST
[/h3]
[i]Gate Zero[/i] is a single-player, third-person story-driven adventure game with an innovative open playstyle that empowers gamers to tackle challenges [i]their [/i]way. As Max, a young teen from a dystopian future thrust into the ancient past, players utilize their own mix of action, stealth, dialogue, unique tools and abilities to save the future and get back to their own time. Do you lean on your evasion and movement skills to charge the Roman guards who’ve taken an interest in the odd stranger in their midst, or do you use stealth and guile to avoid capture and accomplish your goals? Perhaps you use your charisma and dialogue to befriend the locals and enlist their help? You decide and make your own path!

[h3]A LAND ON THE BRINK OF UPHEAVAL
[/h3]Two historic cultures collide when the storied, ancient Jewish homeland is occupied by the preeminent force of the time – The Roman Empire.  Tensions flare as a young rabbi enters an already precarious situation and challenges both forces with his radical new teaching. As Max’s story intersects history, experience firsthand the events of first century Judea with Jesus and his band of followers challenging the authorities and traditions of the time in a first of its kind video game based on historically and Biblically accurate events.

[h3]EXPERIENCE THE REVOLUTION WITH YOUR FRIENDS
[/h3]With[i] Gate Zero’s[/i] revolutionary co-play feature players can bring their friends along for the journey right there beside them. More than spectators, your friends can take on challenges and play on their own mobile devices assisting Max, as the “man in the chair,” guiding him live from the future, as he explores ancient Judea and overcomes the obstacles of life in and around first century Jerusalem, and defeats the enemies sent from the future to stop him. Fill a room with your friends and experience gaming together in a completely new way!

[h3]A PERFECT PARTNERSHIP
[/h3]“From our first meeting with John Gibson, he immediately understood how unique the [i]Gate Zero [/i]project was and saw the enormous potential and vision of creating the world’s first high-quality video game based on the Bible,” said Arve Solli, Head of Studio at Bible X. “With over two decades of experience in releasing successful titles, he has a trained eye for both quality and fun gameplay, combined with a straightforward and practical approach to making a commercially successful product. We truly look forward to bringing the game through the final stages of production and delivering it to millions of players by partnering with Templar Media.”

“I couldn’t be more excited to re-enter games and entertainment at this critical turning point for the industry,” said Templar Media CEO John Gibson. “For too long entertainment has been dominated by one perspective, with the desires of gamers for creators to focus on the fun and put entertainment first being mostly ignored, and with great projects and talented individuals being pushed to the wayside. That ends now with Templar Media’s ‘Entertainment First!’ philosophy as the company seeks out the most talented creators and developers and funds those projects to successfully bring them to market. [i]Gate Zero[/i] is exactly that kind of title, and we couldn’t be more proud to be working with the team to bring this innovative and exciting project to gamers around the world!”

[h3]WE ARE HIRING![/h3]
[i]Gate Zero[/i] is also hiring! If you’re passionate about game development and want to contribute to an exciting project that blends faith and cutting-edge gameplay, reach out to us at [url=mailto:hey@biblex.io]hey@biblex.io[/url].

[h3]STAY CONNECTED
[/h3]To stay updated on the latest developments for [i]Gate Zero[/i], visit our official website and follow us on Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, and Discord. If you’d like to support the development of [i]Gate Zero[/i], you can contribute via the [url=https://nextgenbiblemedia.org/projects/]NextGen Bible Media website[/url].

Together with Templar Media, we are committed to making [i]Gate Zero[/i] a landmark game that brings biblical history to life for a new generation. Stay in touch so you can experience this incredible journey with us!

notes.title: Development Update Dec 2024-Jan 2025
notes.content:
We have successfully entered 2025, looking back on a year filled with prototyping, iterations, and discovering new answers! A huge thank you to everyone who likes, shares, donates, and patiently waits for our Bible video game.

We know a lot of you have followed along with us for a long time, and we acknowledge the fact that updates have been sparse, the reason being that we’ve focused on maintaining momentum behind the scenes!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/96576f11265716ff4618a93b4d37df16ec65c22d.png[/img][i]Concept art for the time traveling realm[/i]

As we mentioned in our previous update, we are currently developing a vertical slice of [i]Gate Zero[/i]; that is, a selected portion of the game, representing the final look and feel. So, to let you all know what’s really going on behind the scenes, we’ve huddled together with the team leads to gain insight into what’s been done, what’s happening, and what’s coming up.

Enjoy our Q&A!

_______________________________________________________________

[h2]Arve Solli (Studio Head)[/h2]

[b]Q: As we begin 2025, GZ has already been up and running for five years. So, where are we in the overall process?
[/b]
A: So far, we’ve done a lot of exploration and development based on input from our community. Now, we’re starting a phase in which everything will come together as we work towards the first release of the game. Our focus has been on creating a game that is not only historically and biblically accurate, but also fun to play and of high quality. This is crucial for us, and we have a solid team of industry veterans with experience from major titles like [i]Assassin’s Creed, GTA, PUBG, Apex Legends, Red Dead Redemption, Diablo, [/i]and more. This amazing team is now bringing all the pieces together!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/abc80c8aa41dbb825e4987523d395e29e4589094.png[/img][i]Some of our awesome team members![/i]

[b]Q: In the previous blog post, we mentioned ramping up for the vertical slice. Which portion of the game does the vertical slice include, and why was this part chosen?
[/b]
A: For the vertical slice, we are creating a section that takes place in the middle of the game. This mission highlights Jesus’ ability to heal—not just physically, but also spiritually. Players will get to explore Capernaum, the town where Jesus lived during the last three years of His life, and experience what it was like to be there.

In addition, it will include some super exciting features that we haven’t shared yet, but will be announced soon!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/377a8fb4b4607899f2087f8c98796c4fcdec4703.png[/img][i]Screen captured scenery of the docks in Capernaum[/i]

[b]Q: A couple of weeks ago, you traveled to the US to meet a handful of the [i]Gate Zero[/i] leads. What was the main goal of the meetup?
[/b]
The main goal of the meetup was to plan and structure the upcoming months of production and ensure that we are set up for success. Our aim is to create the first ever high-quality Bible video game, and this meeting was essential for planning the production phase, diving into the details of design questions and making sure everything is moving forward efficiently.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/10e7e1c643b016525d0a4de8a8f293b5e15c3bb9.png[/img][i]John, Race, and Liam are analyzing the next steps of our current game build[/i]


[h2]Liam Hislop (Senior Producer)[/h2]

[b]Q: You’ve been on the team as our Senior Producer for a few months now – what has it been like?[/b]

A: It’s been a lot of fun and hard work. Getting a handle on the game, while dealing with people remotely is a challenge, but having a great team makes it easier. I think having a design summit, helped us get a really strong, unified vision for the team going forward. [i](More about the design summit below.)[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/28b6d5869744f887b1888d4914dd3d78a86f8b54.png[/img][i]Arve and Liam during the US meetup[/i]

[b]Q: What’s your plan to ensure that things will get done and the next milestones are reached?[/b]

A: Prioritization and accountability. Getting our tasks visible and prioritized with people in different time zones is always the way to overcome the challenges. Also focusing on the core of the game; understanding what makes it really fun and engaging, and making sure those features are solid before we spend time in other areas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/8e51dd1d25155c06ef441788c4ae83290c75ade8.png[/img][i]A map showing where everyone on our team is working from across the world.[/i]


[h2]Kim-David Ostgård (Game Design & UI)[/h2]

[b]Q: As Liam mentioned, the GDs worked together on an online design summit. What was the goal of the summit, and did you achieve that goal?
[/b]
A: That’s right! Being remote and spread across different time zones can be challenging. We recognized the need to bring the design team together to align on the various prototyped elements and make key decisions about the game’s overall direction. The summit was a great success! We made significant progress in aligning our goals, made important design decisions, and updated our Game Design Document to support development in the weeks and months ahead.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/0b1766fefed6e291509114a1b87ed3ee6439aceb.png[/img][i]Game map of Capernaum, with key locations for the Vertical Slice, creating a rich game world[/i]

[b]Q: People might have seen prototype pictures of colorful glitches and crystal formations. What are they, and how do they relate to the story of Jesus?[/b]

A: As many may know, Max travels back in time, and on that note, we’ve been experimenting with different realms of time that players can encounter throughout the game. While this aspect is still a work in progress, we already have some exciting ideas and strong design foundations that help us craft engaging gameplay for different player types! We’re very much looking forward to revealing more as development progresses!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/8de705c1cfec2437d55a6884386d3ff6f32eac28.gif[/img]
[i]Level concept of the time travel realm[/i]


[h2]Steve Chadwick (Game Writer & Actor)[/h2]

[b]Q: One of the big milestones has been writing and recording motion capture for some of the most important cut scenes for the vertical slice. What are your key takeaways from this process?[/b]

[olist]
[*] We will only succeed in touching people’s hearts with our game if, in addition to detailed research, exciting scripts, and immersive gameplay, we capture the drama and emotional impact of these monumental events.
[*] Challenges can always be overcome when team members are passionate about the project.
[*] If you begin with a film script, halve its length. Then halve it again. Finally, refine it so you use about ten percent of what remains, and you might be in the right ballpark for a video game.
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/b06a45c12755cec5062815bd69293a64893c8d61.png[/img][i]Steve prepping the actors for their cut scene[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/9a86cebf22b47da30627637f68f0e4806d2c2d11.gif[/img]
[i]Motion Capture studio in Moss, Norway[/i]


[h2]Markus Paasila Fjeld (Lead Animator)[/h2]

[b]Q: You’re currently working on implementing the motion capture data for the iconic story of the paralytic man lowered through the roof. Have there been any challenges so far?[/b]

A: There are plenty of technical challenges when using mocap for games. One of those is that the actor for the paralytic man was recorded lying on the ground, but I have to make it appear as if he is being carried by four people. For that, I have to create a rig in 3D that can balance on the shoulders of four characters, attach the paralytic man to it, and give the impression of a heavy weight being carried.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/3199cf559318f83e952bafd893810facf548c3a3.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/8cd23ff66265b4953327cfd2052ec7831c7fa280.png[/img][i]Combining several takes of motion capture in Unreal Engine[/i]


[h2]Bobby Bogdanov (Art Director)[/h2]

[b]Q: What recent achievement of the art team are you most proud of?[/b]

A: 2024 was a dynamic year, not only because of content we created, but because we assembled an awesome team of experienced professionals ready to handle any future challenges. We established the technical art pipeline that will enable us to bring the vision for the game to a wide variety of platforms. Last but not least, we advanced significantly with visual development of Capernaum and it’s residents – meeting historical accuracy while ensuring the attractiveness and variety that the present day player expects to see in a high profile game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/0b812b1d12691d6ea2de17e6111c6f5429d2a12e.png[/img][i]Capernaum modules from a year ago (January 2024)[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/dfeba08e34750c4a90f9dd5da37314ec87588799.png[/img][i]Most recent modules, creating the Capernaum marketplace (January 2025)[/i]

[b]Q: How is it like working on an title like [i]Gate Zero[/i], in comparison to games from AAA studios?[/b]

A: I personally always wanted to apply the knowledge and skills of creating rich, engaging open worlds outside the context of big studios and AAA productions. For everyone on the team it is both nostalgic and exciting to work on such a project.


[h2]Daniel Nielsen (Sound Design)[/h2]

[b]Q: What’s the vision or goal for the audio side of things for [i]Gate Zero[/i] this year?[/b]

A: My personal ambitions are to make the sounds of ancient Israel as realistic as possible so it feels like you really are there. Unfortunately, no one on the team has access to a time machine and can walk around in Capernaum 2,000 years ago. So, we try to craft the soundscape with as much care and detail as possible. With help of our archaeological team, we can pinpoint which birds and wildlife sounds to include in the nature ambience. By collaborating closely with the writers team, we can bring the marketplace at the synagogue to life with custom-written background chatter.

When we started using the software [i]Wwise [/i]for [i]Gate Zero[/i] this month, everything immediately seemed much easier. The music systems that we previously spent weeks developing in [i]Unreal Engine[/i], were suddenly done in half a day in [i]Wwise[/i]. I’m particularly excited since Wwise is the leading industry standard for providing audio solutions of the highest quality. We can now design better audio than ever before.

[previewyoutube=XSdWKOuZqFA;full][/previewyoutube][i]Preview of sound effects to be imported through Wwise.[/i]


[h2]Chrys Piva (Lead Programmer)[/h2]

[b]Q: With a background working for studios like [i]Rockstar, Ubisoft [/i]and [i]WB Games[/i], what has it been like getting into the systems and code of [i]Gate Zero[/i]?[/b]

A: The project needed to move from a prototyping mentality and development style over to a more structured production-ready approach for the various game features that have been experimented with.

Over the past months we spent a lot of time creating systems that are scalable and flexible to produce an ambitious open world game like [i]Gate Zero[/i]. Doing so with a very small team has been a major challenge.

We also have to keep performance and ease of debugging in mind. Over the past four months we essentially took the learnings from the prototype project and started building the systems from the ground up to ensure we are hitting all the necessary goals to deliver the game the team has envisioned and that the players deserve.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/a8a9f81df91427d2fc2db4961489780a45b18850.gif[/img][i]This system automatically decides where the Roman guards should position themselves around Max, our main character.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/e925b3f3be7fcd205c627f8ef51d647961f5f930.gif[/img][i]Dynamic crowd systems allow us to create lively environments without working on each NPC character manually.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/a783b4d30bd7f5ec3cd0681c36ec5b1b8cc7abdb.gif[/img]
[i]Early version of a compass system, guiding the player where to go next.[/i]


[h2]Robert Pledger (Major Gift Officer)[/h2]

[b]Q: How is the fundraising going for the first release of [i]Gate Zero[/i], and what steps are being taken to reach full funding?[/b]

In 2025, we will continue working hard on securing enough funds. We have some exciting events and campaigns planned for 2025, and we’ll be taking a more hands-on approach in finding new leads and potential donors. We have also worked on some new marketing material to showcase just how great [i]Gate Zero[/i] is.

Through God’s blessing, faithful service, and due diligence, we continue to be led to high-capacity donors who have a heart for increasing Bible literacy and spreading the gospel worldwide.

[i]“Pray like it all depends on God. Work like it all depends on you.”
[/i]– St. Augustine

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/914205968e2ef5fe924f1eafb8873a256132b021.png[/img][i]In 2024, [i]Gate Zero[/i] was featured at Mehr in Germany and for the first time at GDC in San Francisco![/i]

[b]Do you want to join us in making an impact in the lives of millions of youth worldwide with the gospel in the gaming space?[/b]

[h3][url=https://nextgenbiblemedia.org/donate/?utm_source=steamupdate&utm_medium=steamupdate&utm_campaign=steamdecjan][b]Click here to make a tax-deductible gift to NextGen Bible Media[/b][/url][/h3]


[h1]Other News
[/h1]
[h2]Playthrough by YouTuber FGTeeV Duddy!
[/h2]

FGTeeV’s content is gaming centered and family friendly, has been active for over a decade and is currently entertaining 24 million subscribers. Full video below:

[previewyoutube=PRTQ2riRvEc;full][/previewyoutube]
We reached out to say thanks, and this was his reply:

[i]“I should be thanking you because this game is so amazing. To be able to mix modern day with a gateway to ancient Biblical times is perfect. Learning history on one of the most important books ever while having fun is a win-win. There are so many normal regular games out there and I’m tired of that genre, I want to play games that will actually make a difference in someone’s life! Your game is an amazing tool for that! I can’t wait to play more!”
[/i]
That wraps up this dev update!

We are determined to continue our work in bringing the message of the Bible to life, and making it accessible to children and youth worldwide through one of the world’s first high-quality Bible video games!

Again – a big thank you for your continual support and patience.

notes.title: Development Update Sep-Nov 2024
notes.content:
We’ve reached the end of 2024, and we can sum it up as a year of deep, focused work – some of which we’ll be showcasing in our next big milestone: our vertical slice. The vertical slice will feature a small portion of our game that reflects the final version.

With many of the core components now in place, we’re excited for what 2025 holds as we head into full-fledged production!

Another milestone this quarter is that Friends of BCC Media Inc., doing business as [url=https://nextgenbiblemedia.org/]NextGen Bible Media[/url]—the nonprofit established to support fundraising for the Gate Zero project—has officially been granted 501(c)(3) status in the US. We’re well on our way with fundraising, having raised ~11% of our budget this year alone.

Our team has grown to 30 members, including the NextGen Bible Media admin team. Happy New Year from all of us! We’re incredible grateful for your continued support and patience as we work to create one of the world’s first high-quality Bible video games.

Keep reading for an update from the past months!

[h2]New Team Members[/h2]
We’ve expanded our team this past year to include talented developers with experience at studios like Rockstar Games and Ubisoft, who have worked on iconic games such as [i]GTA[/i], [i]Red Dead Redemption[/i], and [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i], ensuring that Gate Zero continues to push the boundaries of quality. New additions include a producer, level designer, texture artist, game designers, game writers, and an art team.

“I am really looking forward to helping bring this fun and unique experience to everyone. I think that this is something really special.” – Liam, Senior Producer

“I’ve always loved history and truth be told, I am looking forward to the struggle of trying to present this historical/biblical past in a way that is fun to experience and explore.” – Race, Lead Game Designer

“I’m more than excited to join this amazing team of talented people and to help create this innovative Bible-based project that’s bigger than myself. I look forward to crafting memorable experiences for players all around the world!” – Gabriel, Level Designer

“Upon joining the team I see a group of incredibly passionate people all with one goal in mind, bringing the word of God to the gaming industry. I can honestly say that I’ve never been more excited than now to partake in something as big and important as this and I'm looking forward to helping contribute to this incredible project!” – Justin, Texture Artist

[h2]Art[/h2]
[h3]Capernaum 3D Models[/h3]
With a lot of the concept art for Capernaum completed, our artists have moved on to creating 3D models of the different locations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/614856452cd5a3b891507f854084e88ce3673531.jpg[/img][i]Capernaum Dock[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/0a214521bdfe5f4e468fb11493bcce3bada5c3a1.jpg[/img][i]Interior of the dock[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/c983cf0c34b4539fce699080fb12756e0b5bb964.jpg[/img]
[i]Watchtower[/i]

We’ve also been working on 3D models of dock area props.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/3efe2374232d852c6d9791c7daf90fff62145261.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/6362fe3aeb90e4b42354044b64092aed9846d147.jpg[/img]

And here’s a look at the progress of the synagogue in Capernaum. Any guesses what stories will take place here?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/44af93611db89821c4b7863ad167082ac55fb139.jpg[/img][i]Capernaum Synagogue[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/d23683fbd6dc19222248ba1d93d1150028565369.jpg[/img][i]Capernaum Synagogue[/i]

[h3]Capernaum Walkthrough[/h3]
Check out an early look of the different components of Capernaum coming together in the game world!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/04503a7cf7eb49b9c74eb45e68b1d08c24dcc5b3.gif[/img]

[h3]Crowd Characters[/h3]
This quarter, we’ve completed 15 high-resolution models of crowd types that can be made into countless different variations. We’re now working on technical implementation to give you an optimized experience of a lively, populated 1st century Capernaum.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/d2885351596d37ec9a6bacca3dab16d8bfc15d19.jpg[/img]

[h3]Technical Art[/h3]
In addition to constant performance testing and improvement, our technical artist has also been working on testing lighting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/8e5ca73f9dc1aad078028f208c03d3972d050ca5.jpg[/img][i]Lighting Exploration in the Capernaum Synagogue[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/0e640f3fa22162589e65c20db7ca409484e9410d.jpg[/img][i]Lighting Exploration in the Capernaum Synagogue[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/3ee1d3530b65f42a492a04060625a70b8259c517.jpg[/img][i]Lighting Exploration in the Capernaum Synagogue[/i]

[h3]Materials & Textures[/h3]
Lots of realistic textures are being added to the collection! Here is a small selection from the Capernaum area.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/4b64a50c2d3a5e7ef23a049c9626ef64bc1b3f5e.jpg[/img][i]Capernaum Residential Area Textures[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/881f1eb7070930a609c3b1f09c7d95fc2bbe1d1a.jpg[/img][i]Capernaum Synagogue Textures[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/a72dc1ff3890db9d9a88e06578454dd555179cee.jpg[/img][i]Ground Textures[/i]

[h2]Game Mechanics[/h2]
Alongside refining the stealth and action elements of our game, we’ve been working on defining the moment-to-moment gameplay – systems like damage, health, stamina, upgrades, rewards and progression.

We’ve also been detailing the discovery elements, as well as the currency, skills, equipment and resources players can use to fully immerse themselves in the ancient world.

[h2]Story[/h2]
Our game writers have wrapped up in-depth research of the [b]Context, Message and Development[/b] for all Main Missions, filling our research database with rich, detailed profiles of characters, events and stories.

This lays the foundation for crafting immersive and impactful scripts that will bring the gospel stories to life in Gate Zero!

[h2]Reading Plan for the Dev Team[/h2]
Last month, our team began an exciting journey together to read all the core biblical texts describing the events in Release 1 of Gate Zero.

Prepared with care by our game writers, the Gate Zero Daily Reading Plan contains stories packed with interesting narratives, monumental events, and growing tension as forces intent on resisting Jesus gain momentum.

To enrich the experience, each day’s reading includes a fascinating fact or insight that provides deeper context to the Bible passages, reflecting the script team’s depth of research.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/3f21143e805a1a29038fb68aec8ec2a950ec2265.png[/img]
[i]We end off every week with a team game of Kahoot, and the winners get pride of place in our virtual office.[/i]

[h2]Fundraising[/h2]
These past months, we have held two campaigns: the [b]October Matching Gift Campaign[/b] and the [b]Giving Tuesday Matching Campaign[/b], both offering the opportunity for every dollar donated to be matched by an anonymous donor.

A project of this scale and quality demands a budget that reflects its excellence. With Christian projects traditionally suffering from low budgets and and thus quality, we are determined to turn the tide and create something the Christian community will be proud of, and in addition captures the attention of the wider gaming community.

[b]Do you want to join us in making an impact in the lives of millions of youth worldwide with the gospel in the gaming space?[/b]

[h3][url=https://nextgenbiblemedia.org/donate/?utm_source=steamupdate&utm_medium=steamupdate&utm_campaign=steamsepnov][b]Click here to make a tax-deductible gift to NextGen Bible Media[/b][/url][/h3]

[h2]Events[/h2]
[h3]Backer Day at our office in Norway[/h3]
Back in September, we hosted some special guests at our office in Moss, Norway – a reward promised to our high-tier backers.

The visitors got to meet the team, playtest our latest gameplay features (top secret!) and participate in an exclusive motion capture session where they saw themselves as NPCs within the game.

[url=https://biblex.io/2024/09/27/gate-zero-backer-day-new-updates-devlog-17/][b]Click here for the writeup and video devlog from the day[/b][/url]

[previewyoutube=8l6iAJ17iCU;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Reach Conf[/h3]
We were proud to be part of the first-ever [url=https://www.reachconf.org/]Reach Conf[/url] in Orlando, FL in September showcasing Gate Zero.

The conference was a reward for the content creators who had organized Alpha groups to share the gospel prior to the event. Creators could invite their community to the conference, and it was a uniting time with lots of games, food and encouragement.

We loved meeting the familiar faces of Christian streamers who love and support our game, as well as new people enthusiastic for what we’re creating. Already looking forward to next year!

notes.title: Development Update Jun-Aug 2024
notes.content:
Summer is slowly making its exit, and while things usually slow down during this time, the important work on our game has not stopped, with a good part of our team working hard through the warm months. Here is a look at our progress in the last bit!

[h2]Art[/h2]
In the past months, we have expanded and strengthened our art team and made significant progress on this front. We have also established collaboration with a team of professionals who have worked on several Assassin’s Creed games, which we hope will take the quality and consistency of our art to the next level.

[h3]Capernaum Concept Art[/h3]
With the exterior concept art done, we have now moved on to designing the interiors.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/aa9d9effcb22f572024f09a03e6cb0d92c9766fa.jpg[/img][i]Concept Art: Rich Building Interior Living Room[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/53666dad79c984c5b367a48e55ee7f5d7886b588.jpg[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Rich Building Interior Living Room[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/703787c23ed08c476cebd91ce125954de0890d79.jpg[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Residential District Kitchen[/i]

[h3]Capernaum Residential Modular Set[/h3]

As we work on building out Capernaum, we have also developed a modular system to improve efficiency and ensure optimized performance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/3b359495488a2dd6e3fec4e2a7b82296387c5383.jpg[/img][i]Capernaum Residential Modular Set[/i]

[h3]Materials & Textures[/h3]

Our artists have also been hard at work with the details, creating materials and textures of building façades like roofs and walls, props such as carpets and pottery, and clothing textiles and fabrics. A lot goes into creating high-quality, realistic graphics which are at the same time optimized for an open world game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/200a75cbc8dbf0ea1a114394d9c6e6a4ace83478.jpg[/img][i]Texture on a building façade[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/28b7abe22a9c716f54caf611587887d5013a66ce.jpg[/img][i]Carpet samples[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/0f7ebb86f7c2ab364fb09a6680af65a9e2f02ba6.jpg[/img]
[i]Textiles[/i]

[h2]Game Mechanics[/h2]
Recently, we’ve made major improvements to the stealth elements of Gate Zero, with the goal of making it fun by incorporating lighthearted, humorous moments. You may just find Max with lots of new tricks up his sleeve as you find creative ways to evade enemies and danger!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/f7a7f5d7249a5ca57b1f549ea0a9ec6b2a9af94b.gif[/img]

We have also been seriously prototyping some action elements for the game, working hard on making them balanced, responsive and fun. The goal is that these new elements will be easy to learn and rewarding to master. We’ve spent a good amount of time getting this right, and we can’t wait to show you more when we’re ready! Stay tuned!

[h2]Level Design[/h2]
Level design is also an important part of game development, and one aspect of it is defining heights and spaces between buildings and other environment assets.

Rules for horizontal and vertical traversal ie. jumping and climbing distances defined for the environment art and level design will ensure a unified, clear and positive player experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/d45c3db21aa7184b80ceb8cfaa66b60d2fa1e882.jpg[/img]
[i]Vertical Traversal Rules[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/6d4914f8d87fb46b55a01a62df6cbe7293569d37.jpg[/img]
[i]Horizontal Traversal Rules[/i]

[h2]Story[/h2]

Our scriptwriters have been doing extensive research into the gospel stories that will be featured in Release 1, determining the context and main messages we aim to bring out through the stories in each mission.

They have also been working on character development of the various people that Max (the player character) will be meeting in the game. It’s shaping up to be incredibly interesting!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/ab41d60714a84171d1fa0dad6693097156a6aaef.png[/img]
[i]Overview of the gospel stories we plan to feature in Release 1[/i]

[h2]Fundraising[/h2]
In case you missed our last blog post or email messages, [b]we are still actively fundraising for Gate Zero.[/b]

Our goal as one of the world’s first Bible video games is to create a product of excellence. The more resources added to the project, the greater impact we can make on millions worldwide with the life-changing message of the gospel.

Creating a video game of this scale and quality with care, respect and attention to the source material takes a considerable amount of resources, and we are grateful for any support you can provide!

[url=https://nextgenbiblemedia.com/projects/][b]If you would like to give to our mission, please visit our donation page here[/b][/url]

[previewyoutube=UaIWmKjQZkI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Events[/h2]
[h3]Forward Conference in Georgia[/h3]
At the end of June, we attended a large youth conference in Georgia where 13,000 young people were gathered. Our Gate Zero booth was a hit with the crowd, and it was so fun to see these young Gen Zers' interest in our game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/788e21bf5d9cd7b465eb77ad6ec00e5824d324dc.png[/img]
[i]Gate Zero booth at Forward Conference 2024[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/b792aa721585501affffac5530f2aceb2ad29421.png[/img]

notes.title: Development Update Mar-May 2024
notes.content:
Time has flown by and although it’s been a quiet few months with fewer updates, our team has been working a lot in the background especially on the game design and programming side, getting the mechanics polished and tightened up so we can create a fun, cohesive and excellent experience for all of you!

Here’s a summary of our work and achievements since March in one BIG update!

[h2]Game Mechanics[/h2]
So far, our team has completed 10 prototyping sprints this year. A sprint is a short, focused period where different design elements are prototyped, tested out and validated before further work is done to incorporate them into the game.

Through this process, our development team has iterated on the dialogue system, discovery and meta loop, traversal, time, stealth and combat elements of our game.

Yes, you read it right – we’ve experimenting with non-lethal combat mechanics. What do you think about that?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/fea5aa7f6b2ee3ff92f40a2c27040d758df3ce68.gif[/img]

Lots of new mechanics have been tested in the past months, and we’re looking forward to revealing more once we’re ready to! We’ve been conducting rounds of playtesting among members of our community, and we’re getting closer to the result!

[h2]Art[/h2]
We’ve made a lot of progress on the art front in recent months. One big milestone we’ve reached is that we’ve now completed concept art of the Capernaum rich district, residential district and Simon Peter’s house, and we’re now moving on to designing landmarks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/5771fdbc9836490d07da62a1c36d84c61d8b69e4.jpg[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Capernaum Residential District[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/3c6efb79af815c959efd6e9ceb9a05f7cc353513.jpg[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Capernaum Rich District[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/a28923f72adf1c849fbed05e69aa3e8c9b572389.jpg[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Capernaum Rich District[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/4570bf7e285a35570edc0abddb94db073661bb5c.jpg[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Simon Peter's House[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/fef4c18b175dcec94c1e451ea87e2953aa15ee59.jpg[/img][i]Concept Art: Simon Peter's House[/i]

We’ve also started implementing the Capernaum rich district buildings into the game world. Check out an early look below!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/9dda992612e53db53ae345f3b6e8cfa48b549fe7.gif[/img]

To prepare for further world-building, we’ve been developing a modular system for buildings, structures, materials and textures to have centralized control over the art, improve efficiency and optimize memory and performance.

Aside from buildings, we’ve also been working closely with our history consultants to develop a solid basis for 1st century characters and clothing as we begin to create concept art for the crowd.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/3a9ed5db2df92ce134b75bb82fa0b0ac958a0bf0.png[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Jewish Rich Male[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/85c3d0c468a8df49cbca09d3b76331c82897fac4.png[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Jewish Regular Female[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/7fca68dd1bbb3f529ada8a7ba52ffa9a49cd869a.png[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Fisherman[/i]

Another thing we’ve been prototyping that we haven’t shown much of yet are World State Effects – alternative renderings to the normal world that indicate a different state the player is in. The world effects are connected to the time travel element of our game and bring yet another exciting dimension to gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/cd9e6806583af9d07c9d4c6482083179b022b887.png[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Time World[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/828432f1f95a15b11b2017a4b2fb8847a247e61f.png[/img]
[i]Concept Art: Corrupted World[/i]

[h2]Research[/h2]

In the past months, we have established a tight, solid collaboration and workflow with our history consultants. Their insight and research is invaluable to the game we are creating, and we are constantly in awe over the rich depth there is to the Bible’s stories both from a historical and archaeological standpoint.

Besides offering input to ensure historical accuracy, we’ve experienced that the amazing teamwork we’ve got going with these historians extends beyond getting the facts right. Knowledge of archaeology and history can also add fun elements to the game’s design and mechanics, for example with the addition of maps, artifacts, caves and environmental obstacles, as well as daily-life habits and tasks of the locals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/4eb0335c8fd92362a6a3f8aff7ec0ee7565eda28.png[/img]
[i]Research board of characters and clothing[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/2e56e5cca15f94fd0b65acc52b4fdc89a280cbbb.png[/img]
[i]Research board of various elements in 1st century Capernaum[/i]

[h2]Team Updates & Office Fun[/h2]

As development progresses, we have also been actively hiring to recruit the necessary talent to complete the game. New additions to the team include a game designer, associate producer, technical artist, texture artist, two level designers, and most recently, a senior game designer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/f068de8afe487806376f1a7a89c723a572f36f9b.png[/img]
[i]As our remote team grows, we’ve found different ways to collaborate and communicate. We now work together in a virtual office using Gather Town.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/467424b535f65fe23518e9eff601eaa399e6e038.png[/img]
[i]Some fun on the office Slack chat[/i]

[h2]Events[/h2]
[h3]Game Developers Conference 2024[/h3]
In March, we brought a Gate Zero booth for the first time to the Game Developers Conference (GDC) in San Francisco. We received overwhelmingly positive feedback and met many awesome people genuinely interested in what we are doing!

[url=https://biblex.io/2024/04/01/gdc-2024/]Read the full GDC report and see the pictures here
[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/8a5b52e5886ad884b637e6301f44a3972425b829.jpg[/img]

[h2]Marketing[/h2]

In March, we hit an exciting milestone: [b]500,000 followers across all social media platforms and 50M combined views![/b] We are overwhelmed with the attention Gate Zero is getting, and humbled and motivated to keep working hard. Thank you SO much for all your continued support and encouragement!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/d7d121b2939e5e0e211b264707ee7fa1124e07cd.jpg[/img]

And with that, we leave you with an awesome piece of fan art created by VoxVulpes from our Discord community.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/04ec76b2b61697cb919e46e4fa517e3e611669b4.png[/img]

notes.title: Development Update Jan-Feb 2024
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

It's been a hot minute but here we are with a comprehensive update!

First of all, we'd like to announce that [b]we'll be attending the [url=https://gdconf.com/]Game Developers Conference (GDC)[/url] next month in San Francisco with a Gate Zero booth[/b]. If you plan to be there, be sure to stop by and say hi!

[h2]Research Efforts[/h2]
What's unique – and challenging at the same time – about making a historical video game as compared to a TV series like [i]The Chosen[/i], is that players get to explore locations [i]just as they were[/i].

From a geographical point of view, this requires much more research to ensure the map is accurate as you can technically [i]choose [/i]to run anywhere you like, while in a TV series, the viewer only sees the locations the camera shoots, and from limited angles at that.

We've taken this unique challenge seriously by doing due diligence in research, at the same time being mindful of the balance between historical accuracy and making a video game that is fun.

[h3]Historical Consulting Sessions[/h3]
Last week, we invited archaeological architect [url=https://www.ritmeyer.com/about/]Leen Ritmeyer[/url] to hold a talk with our team about daily life in Capernaum. Leen's reconstruction drawings of Capernaum and designs of 1st century homes have been an big source of inspiration for us.

One piece of advice he gave: "Do not look at life in 1st century Capernaum with your 21st century ideas." It was an incredibly insightful talk, and we're looking forward to incorporating the knowledge in our script, art and game design!

In addition, we've received over three hours of video research from historical consultants in the past week about character references and clothing from the 1st century, so our art team has been busy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/e9c556cf039dced39903c2c65442bb62dc513293.jpg[/img]
[i]Members of our team attending a talk with archaeological architect Leen Ritmeyer
[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/575530d01abd42f9b74ac4917e0a89dd2e5cb2b4.jpg[/img]
[i]Our script team was visiting from the UK and also got to attend the talk at our office in Norway
[/i]

[h2]Capernaum Art + Fun Facts[/h2]
These days, our small but hardworking art team has been working closely with our archaeological consultants to ensure accuracy as they continue building the town of Capernaum.

[h3]Fun facts about Capernaum:[/h3]
[list]
[*] The 1st century synagogue of Capernaum where Jesus taught at was never excavated, so no one knows for sure what it looked like.
[*] Fishing was quite a profitable industry. It was an elaborate business that could involve employees mending nets, maintaining boats, preserving, transporting and selling fish.
[*] Torah scrolls were often kept in the house of the Ruler of the Synagogue and brought in a cart to the synagogue where they were read.
[/list]
We've learned an innumerable amount of detail concerning architecture and life in Capernaum during Jesus' time, but we won't bore you with the nitty-gritty... Instead, we'll show you some results!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/00e6aa485db4f7a4e58cec6628780a94c7c103c3.jpg[/img]
[i]A redesigned version of the Capernaum synagogue following feedback from historians
[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/dddf729ba77415376546f0495d7af7d705604a33.jpg[/img]
[i]Mood exploration for the streets of Capernaum
[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/fdf25599a75992de5f33a4bd855644661a9bbfaa.jpg[/img]
[i]Mood exploration for the streets of Capernaum
[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/b6708c14ae7b19121b1f83e9a9a7e92491ed6fdf.jpg[/img]
[i]WIP concept art of the residential district in Capernaum
[/i]

[h2]Game Mechanics Prototype[/h2]

Our prototype team has been working hard experimenting with game mechanics, and this past week, we had a new round of closed testing among members of our community. We'll show more of what we're working on when we're ready!

In the meantime, here's a funny bug our head of studio Arve discovered...

[h2]New Executive Game Consultant[/h2]

We started this year off welcoming John Gibson as our new Executive Game Consultant and [i]Gate Zero[/i] Development Board Member.

John brings two decades of experience and expertise in game development and publishing to our team. As former CEO, co-owner, and co-founder of Tripwire Interactive, he led the team that brought hit games like [i]Killing Floor[/i], [i]Maneater[/i], and [i]Chivalry 2[/i] to market, selling tens of millions of copies and winning multiple game of the year awards.

John has been offering support and counsel to our team in the past months, and will continue to provide guidance throughout our project's milestones and pivotal decisions. Following advice from John, we have also evaluated increasing the budget and quality of [i]Gate Zero[/i] to ensure the highest possible success.

[url=https://biblex.io/2024/01/18/announcing-john-gibson-as-executive-game-consultant/]Read the official announcement here[/url]

[h2]Social Media Growth[/h2]
This month, we hit another milestone on Instagram: Reaching [b]5.2 million[/b] and gaining [b]65,824 followers[/b] in [b]just one week![/b]

In total, we have reached[b] over 14 million[/b] unique accounts on Instagram since we first went viral in October last year. Word about our game is spreading more than we can imagine, and we're so excited to see where all this is headed in the coming year!

notes.title: Development Update Nov-Dec 2023
notes.content:
Happy New Year! Just like that, 2023 is over. The last couple months of 2023 have been busy and eventful for us here at Bible X, with progress being made on all fronts especially art, game design and marketing. Here's an update on what we've been working on!

[h1]Game Mechanics – Traversal Experimentation[/h1]
In the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1748280/view/5480376121642346366]last update[/url], we announced that we’ve been intensely prototyping and working on improving the game mechanics in Gate Zero. This has been the focus of our design and programming teams for the past few months with one goal: to make the moment-to-moment gameplay so fun that players want to engage with our game again and again.

One of the areas we’ve been testing out are traversal actions for the player character. Here’s a clip from a little test of Max using a shepherd’s staff. What do you think?

[previewyoutube=DbrvYOttHlM;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Capernaum[/h2]
Capernaum is a crucial location mentioned multiple times in all four gospels. It is the home base of Jesus when He began His public ministry, and is often referred to as His second home. Some key places include the house of Simon Peter’s mother-in-law, the Sea of Galilee and the synagogue where Jesus taught.

Our art team has been busy moving from the concept art stage to building Capernaum in Unreal Engine 5. Throughout the process, we consult with historians to ensure historical accuracy. Many elements here will need a lot more work, but we wanted to share the beautiful art our team has been creating so far!

[h2]Capernaum Docks[/h2]

[h2]Sea of Galilee[/h2]

[previewyoutube=4m-eJgTFewA;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Instagram Viral Success[/h1]
In October, [url=https://www.instagram.com/biblexgame/]our Instagram[/url] broke records.[b] Over 9.5 MILLION people[/b] have now seen Gate Zero content in the last 90 days on Instagram! We also saw a [b]5x follower growth[/b] since October, and we're currently at 128,000 followers! [url=https://biblex.io/2023/12/11/how-to-go-viral-on-instagram/]We wrote a post-mortem detailing some stats and lessons learned here.[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/704e96d9d3d9ef57be6338ba6b7135e5cbed82c3.png[/img]

[h1]Would you like to further support our mission?[/h1]
Bible X, as a part of the media organization BCC Media, is a non-profit game studio. Donations to Bible X are tax-deductible. If you would like to make a year-end gift to support our mission to bring the Bible to the next generation, we invite you to [b][url=https://biblex.io/donate/?utm_source=bxwebsite&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=decupdate]check out our giving page here.[/url][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43975417/88ab40d6bd1b42f7abbe22cc2da379d31cba8044.gif[/img]

And that’s it for now! We hope you've had a wonderful Christmas and New Year. Thank you for all your support for Gate Zero in 2023, and we look forward to sharing more in the year to come!
